standard_prerequisites.name: Definition 4.2 (def:good rectangle, good geometric rectangles)
standard_prerequisites.statement: Source lines 591-604: for c in GX and tau >> 1, with U^- x U^+ a product inside the open set partial(c,tau) of endpoint pairs (source lines 585-589), the good geometric rectangle R(c,tau; U^-,U^+) consists of the geodesics with prescribed endpoints; the maximal version is R(c,tau); open and closed variants are used, and by compactness of hat GX finitely many flow-shrunk open rectangles cover it.
standard_prerequisites.use: The building blocks of the constructed family: the statement produces D_i of the form g_{s_i}R_i with R_i a good geometric rectangle, and the proof covers hat GX by flow-shrunk open rectangles of diameter < rho (proof line 902); declared as a navigation pointer.

standard_prerequisites.name: Definition 3.5 (defn:proper, proper family) and Definition 3.7 (defn:pollicott, pre-Markov proper family)
standard_prerequisites.statement: Source section 3: a proper family (B,D) for the flow at scale alpha is a pair of collections of rectangles satisfying (1) diam D_i < alpha and B_i subset D_i, (2) the union of g_{(-alpha,0)} Int_g B_i covers the space, (3) the separation condition for local orbit segments (items labelled defn:proper1/2/3 inside the definition); a pre-Markov proper family (Definition 3.7) additionally satisfies the Markovian transition condition eq (premarkov, printed 3.1).
standard_prerequisites.use: The proposition produces a pre-Markov proper family at scale alpha; the proof checks the three conditions of Definition 3.5 (item references \eqref{defn:proper1}/2/3 carried as item stubs of Definition 3.5) and then applies Lemma 4.11 to obtain the pre-Markov property of Definition 3.7 (proof line 916).

standard_prerequisites.name: Lemma 4.11 (markovpf, the bridge lemma)
standard_prerequisites.statement: Source lines 782-784: let (phi_t) be a Lipschitz continuous expansive flow on a compact metric space; given a proper family (B,D) for (phi_t) at scale alpha > 0 where the B_i and D_i are rectangles, there exists a pre-Markov proper family (B',D') at scale alpha > 0 such that every D'_k in D' is the image under phi_{s_k} of some D_i in D, where |s_k| << alpha.
standard_prerequisites.use: Invoked at proof line 916 to convert the recursively built proper family into a pre-Markov one; the intervening lemma sits between the proposition's statement and proof in the source (its own proof is lines 788-896) and is not part of the counted span; declared as a navigation pointer.

standard_prerequisites.name: Lemma 2.4 (lem:X GX bound) and Lemma 4.7 (lem:deform tool)
standard_prerequisites.statement: Lemma 2.4 (source lines 253-255) provides the constant L bounding the displacement of geodesics under the flow; Lemma 4.7 (source lines 715-717) is the deformation tool: for rectangular subsets R_1, R_2 of good geometric rectangles with diam(R_1) = epsilon, flow-shifted copies g_t T with t, t' farther than 2L epsilon apart are disjoint from a fixed rectangle they once touched.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof picks epsilon << rho/(4Ll) with L from Lemma 2.4 (proof line 910) and uses Lemma 4.7 to pick the distinct times s_k in (0,rho) with g_{s_k}T_k disjoint from all D_j (proof line 912); Lemma 4.7 is this lane's next card, so both are declared as navigation pointers.

standard_prerequisites.name: Standard inputs
standard_prerequisites.statement: Convex cocompact locally CAT(-kappa) space X and its geodesic flow (g_t) on GX (compact case) or hat GX (otherwise); local orbit segments (all orbits of length 8 alpha local for alpha small); compactness of hat GX giving finite subcovers; closed subsets of products of endpoint sets identified via geodesic endpoints.
standard_prerequisites.use: Standing geometric input of section 4; not reproduced beyond the author's own text.

core_obligations: State the proposition (statement lines 776-778): let X be a convex cocompact locally CAT(-kappa) space and (g_t) its geodesic flow (on GX when X is compact, on hat GX otherwise); for any sufficiently small alpha > 0 there exists a pre-Markov proper family (B,D) for the flow at scale alpha such that each D_i has the form g_{s_i}R_i for some s_i with |s_i| << alpha and some good geometric rectangle R_i.

Setup and start of the recursion (proof line 902): choose alpha so that all orbits of length 8 alpha are local and fix rho much smaller than alpha; for each c in hat G tilde X pick an open good geometric rectangle of diameter < rho; the flow-shrunk family {g_{(-rho,0)} tilde R(c,tau)} covers hat G tilde X, so by compactness of hat GX a finite family tilde H_1,...,tilde H_n (tilde H_i = g_{(-rho,0)} tilde R_i) has projections H_i = g_{(-rho,0)}R_i covering hat GX; start with B_1 subset D_1 a closed good geometric rectangle of diameter < alpha with R_1 inside Int_g B_1, so H_1 subset g_{(-alpha,0)} Int_g B_1.

Recursive step and the leftover set (proof lines 904-910): suppose (B_j,D_j)_{j=1}^l chosen with diam D_j < alpha, D_j pairwise disjoint, each D_j of the form g_{s_j}R_i with |s_i| << alpha; let H_i be the smallest-index cover element not contained in the union of g_{[-alpha,0]} Int_g B_j; define the leftover set M_i = { c in R_i : g_{(0,rho)}c cap (union_j Int_g B_j) = empty } = R_i setminus (union_j g_{(-rho,0)} Int_g B_j) (display, proof lines 906-909); M_i is a closed subset of R_i; pick epsilon << rho/(4Ll) with L from Lemma 2.4; via geodesic endpoints M_i is identified with a closed subset of U^- x U^+, so finitely many closed rectangles T_1,...,T_n with T_k identified with V_k^- x V_k^+ have {Int_g T_k} covering M_i, T_k cap M_i nonempty, and diam T_k < epsilon.

Choosing the time shifts (proof line 912): by Lemma 4.7, if g_t T_k cap D_j is nonempty for some t in [0,rho], then g_{t'}T_k and D_j are disjoint for |t'-t| > 2L epsilon; since 4L epsilon << rho/l and at most l of the D_j can intersect g_{[0,rho]}T_k, one picks distinct s_k in (0,rho) with g_{s_k}T_k disjoint from the union of the D_j.

Extension and verification (proof lines 914-916): add D_k := g_{s_k}T^k to the collection and choose inside each new D_k a slightly smaller closed rectangle B_k so that {g_{-s_k} Int_g B_k} covers M_i; since rho < alpha the enlarged family covers H_i; iterating until hat GX is covered by {g_{(-alpha,0)} Int_g B_j}, the proof checks the conditions of Definitions 3.5 and 3.7: condition (2) is ensured by construction, condition (1) holds by the Lipschitz property of the flow and epsilon << alpha (diam D_j < alpha), condition (3) holds by the disjoint construction and the 8 alpha-local choice of alpha; applying Lemma 4.11 produces a pre-Markov proper family satisfying Definition 3.7, and by construction each D_i is the image of a good geometric rectangle under the flow for a small time.
proof_roadmap: State the proposition: pre-Markov proper families at any small scale, each D_i a small flow-image of a good geometric rectangle (statement lines 776-778).
Cover hat GX by finitely many flow-shrunk open good rectangles and start the recursion with one closed rectangle B_1 (proof line 902).
For the first uncovered cover element, form the closed leftover set M_i inside R_i and discretize it by finitely many small closed rectangles T_k (proof lines 904-910).
